# Bring client-rust to behavioral parity with client-go

This ExecPlan is a living document. Keep `Progress`, `Surprises & Discoveries`, `Decision Log`, and `Outcomes & Retrospective` up to date as work proceeds.

Reference: TiDB's `PLANS.md` at `/Users/qiliu/projects/tidb/PLANS.md`; this plan is maintained according to that format because this is a correctness-sensitive, multi-package transcreation.

## Purpose / Big Picture

The goal is for Rust applications using `tikv-client` to observe the same TiKV protocol behavior as applications using `github.com/tikv/client-go/v2`, while keeping an idiomatic Rust API. `client-go` is the behavioral source of truth. Completion is demonstrated package by package with an inventory, an explicit Rust integration decision, ported tests or equivalent differential tests, and the relevant unit and real-cluster validation gates.

This is not a textual Go-to-Rust rewrite. A Go package is the minimum claim unit. A package is not marked complete until every production file, platform or generated input, original test/support artifact, fixture, build implication, and validation gate has been accounted for. A package that depends on unimplemented behavior remains `seed` or `blocked`, never `complete`.

## Surprises & Discoveries

- Observation: the repositories have different architectural boundaries. Client-go has roughly sixty Go package directories and 274 Go files, while client-rust is primarily one crate whose request planning, PD, store, raw, and transaction modules cross several Go package boundaries.
  Evidence: client-go package inventory in `doc/client-go-parity-ledger.md`; client-rust modules under `src/`.

- Observation: client-rust currently accepts any `u32` keyspace ID and overwrites its high byte when constructing the four-byte API-v2 prefix. Client-go rejects IDs above `0xFFFFFF`.
  Evidence: client-go `internal/apicodec/codec_v2.go:getIDByte`; client-rust `src/request/keyspace.rs:keyspace_prefix`.

- Observation: client-rust forms an unbounded API-v2 range end by evaluating `keyspace_id + 1`. At ID `0xFFFFFF`, debug builds overflow and release builds can form the wrong prefix. Client-go increments the complete four-byte mode-plus-ID prefix, producing `r ff ff ff` to `s 00 00 00` for raw mode.
  Evidence: client-go `internal/apicodec/codec_v2.go:NewCodecV2`; client-rust `src/request/keyspace.rs:EncodeKeyspace for BoundRange`.

- Observation: several small source packages are architecturally coupled in Rust. `internal/client/mockserver` needs server-side tonic generation while client-rust currently generates clients only; `internal/logutil.Hex` needs protobuf reflection/descriptor support; and `tikvrpc/interceptor` needs transaction/snapshot-to-transport propagation.
  Evidence: client-go package sources and consumers; client-rust `proto-build/src/main.rs`, `src/store/client.rs`, and generated `tikvpb.rs`.

- Observation: `config/retry` budgets cumulative sleep and tracks classified errors, cancellation, kill signals, and forked accounting, whereas client-rust's current `Backoff` limits attempts only.
  Evidence: client-go `config/retry/backoff.go` and tests; client-rust `src/backoff.rs` and request-plan loops.

- Observation: `internal/resourcecontrol` cannot be completed as an isolated context helper because its request consumption logic switches on `tikvrpc.Request` command types and its mode is selected by `config.NextGen`.
  Evidence: client-go `internal/resourcecontrol` production sources and their imports; the corresponding Rust RPC wrapper/config contracts remain unassessed.

- Observation: the small `testutils` package contains only aliases and factories over concrete mocktikv types, while the `error` package's write-conflict construction and diagnostics depend on metrics and log utilities.
  Evidence: client-go `testutils/mockstore.go` and both files under `error`; these rows are now explicit seeds rather than misleading small standalone candidates.

- Observation: client-go exposes transaction command priority through `txnkv/txnutil`, `KVTxn.SetPriority`, and snapshot request contexts. Client-rust's protobuf contains `Context.priority`, but no public Rust priority type or transaction option sets it.
  Evidence: client-go `txnkv/txnutil/priority.go`, `txnkv/transaction/txn.go`, and `txnkv/txnsnapshot/snapshot.go`; client-rust `src/generated/kvrpcpb.rs` and `src/store/request.rs`.

- Observation: `oracle/oracles` owns a reusable cache/validation state machine, but its concrete PD transport and high-level construction cross the `internal/client`, `tikv`, and metrics package boundaries. Deterministic timestamp sources cover the package contract without needing unistore; real-cluster PD interoperability remains on those owning rows.
  Evidence: client-go `oracle/oracles/pd.go`, `tikv/kv.go`, and `metrics/metrics.go`; client-rust `src/oracle/oracles.rs`, `src/pd/{client,retry,cluster}.rs`, and `src/stats.rs`.

## Decision Log

- Decision: pin both repositories at the revisions observed at project start.
  Rationale: `master` is moving; reproducible behavioral claims require immutable source inputs. Later upstream refreshes will be separate ledger updates.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: preserve idiomatic Rust public APIs while matching protocol semantics, defaults, error conditions, retry effects, and observable ordering.
  Rationale: copying Go type shapes mechanically would make the Rust library less usable without improving wire compatibility.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: complete `txnkv/txnutil` before API-v2 codec work.
  Rationale: it is a complete, small source package with a direct missing Rust wire behavior. `internal/apicodec` depends on a broader RPC command inventory and cannot honestly be claimed complete as the first milestone.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: record partial discoveries such as the maximum-keyspace bug as `seed` evidence until their entire Go package reaches its completion gate.
  Rationale: repository policy forbids reporting partial functions or branches as transcreated packages.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: represent client-go's automatic `race` build tag with an explicit `race-tests` Cargo feature.
  Rationale: stable Rust has no automatic ThreadSanitizer cfg equivalent; an explicit feature makes both build states deterministic and allows sanitizer commands and CI jobs to select the race-specific test behavior.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: represent client-go's `intest` build tag with an `internal-tests` Cargo feature and its mutable global with atomic accessors.
  Rationale: Cargo features are the native build-variant mechanism, while an atomic preserves runtime test override behavior without introducing the data race possible through direct mutable globals.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: collapse `util/redact.String` and its private encoding helpers into safe Rust key formatting rather than expose arbitrary bytes as a Rust `String`.
  Rationale: the Go helper is only called on newly hex-encoded ASCII and has no external repository consumer; arbitrary non-UTF-8 bytes cannot inhabit a safe Rust `String`. Uppercase hexadecimal and redaction outputs remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: keep `internal/mockstore/cluster` as an internal Rust test-support trait and leave its concrete implementation to the separate `internal/mockstore/mocktikv` milestone.
  Rationale: the source package contains only the interface; its sole production implementer and all state-transition behavior live in a distinct Go package. Preserving that ownership avoids overclaiming mock-store behavior while still completing every interface method and type contract atomically.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: represent `kv.LockCtx`'s cross-package statistics pointer with an object-safe typed marker and defer the statistics payload/merge implementation to `util`.
  Rationale: `kv` only carries the pointer; defining observability behavior here would violate the source package boundary. `Any` access lets the eventual native statistics type be recovered without weakening thread safety.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: represent Go `context.Context` in the standalone trace package with an immutable type-keyed Rust `TraceContext`, and preserve arbitrary zap field payloads through typed `Any` values.
  Rationale: client-rust has no shared Go-style context object. Type-keyed immutable derivation preserves the source's value/extractor and nesting semantics, while typed fields avoid reducing structured trace data to formatted strings.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: complete the interface-only `oracle` package independently from the concrete `oracle/oracles` package.
  Rationale: the source package owns only contracts, timestamp transformations, a noop validator, and error values. PD/local allocation, caching, expiration, staleness, and validation algorithms are separate source-package artifacts and remain atomic on their own ledger row.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: map the blocking latch scheduler to a mutex-serialized async scheduler with one-shot notifications and RAII/cancellation cleanup, while preserving source slot and queue semantics.
  Rationale: blocking a Tokio executor thread would be non-native and can deadlock low-thread runtimes. The native mapping preserves acquisition/wakeup/staleness observations and adds safe dropped-future cleanup without changing successful transaction ordering.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: expose client-go's dynamic error package as typed, downcastable Rust errors in a public `error` module while retaining the crate's root transport error as an integration wrapper.
  Rationale: one monolithic enum would erase Go-style concrete type checks and make protobuf-backed payloads awkward. Typed errors preserve field access and predicates; transparent root wrapping integrates conditions returned by current high-level APIs.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

- Decision: extend client-rust's existing non-exhaustive `Config` rather than introduce a parallel Go-shaped root configuration, and map the `nextgen` build tag to a Cargo feature.
  Rationale: one configuration object keeps current Rust constructors compatible while exposing every source default and validation contract. Rust ownership, non-negative durations, and kebab-case serde remain native boundaries; protocol-affecting values and source-hidden fields retain source behavior.
  Date/Author: 2026-08-23 / Codex

## Outcomes & Retrospective

Eighteen packages are complete at the pinned client-go revision. Foundational state/memory, typed errors, configuration, concrete oracle behavior, mock test-support contracts, and the native union-store core remain validated; local optimistic commits use the complete client-go latch behavior through native async scheduling. Consumer behavior remains explicitly attached to retry, routing, snapshots, transactions, metrics, concrete mock-store, and high-level oracle construction rows. The current Rust validation baseline is 167 library tests and 49 doctests, plus scoped all-feature clippy and rustfmt. None of these eighteen package contracts requires a real cluster because their own observable behavior is deterministic state, memory, configuration, build, interface, callbacks, batching, scheduling, protobuf-context, error transformation, or byte transformation; consumer protocol integration still does.

## Context and Orientation

The source repository is `/private/tmp/client-go` at commit `52c1e76cec993571493c81de442bcbef90cdc106`. It is read-only evidence. The implementation repository is `/Users/qiliu/projects/client-rust` on branch `codex/client-go-parity`, based on commit `0ebb6b91a50684aeb07383a500033955e3bcfeb3`. Its `origin` is `https://github.com/ngaut/client-rust.git`; `upstream` is `https://github.com/tikv/client-rust.git`.

In client-go, `txnkv/txnutil/priority.go` defines normal, low, and high TiKV command priority and converts them to `kvrpcpb.CommandPri`. Transactions store this priority, snapshots inherit it, and request construction writes it into `kvrpcpb.Context.Priority`. In client-rust, all TiKV requests implement `store::Request` through the macro in `src/store/request.rs`; that macro already writes leader and API-version context. `TransactionOptions` in `src/transaction/transaction.rs` is the idiomatic point for selecting transaction behavior, while `Transaction`, `Snapshot`, `SyncTransaction`, and `SyncSnapshot` are the user-facing execution objects.

“Differential test” means sending equivalent operations through Go and Rust clients to the same clean cluster and comparing protocol-visible results, errors, ordering, and state. Unit equivalence is preferred for deterministic helpers; real-cluster equivalence is required where mocks cannot establish the behavior.

## Plan of Work

First, implement the complete `txnkv/txnutil` package contract. Add a Rust `Priority` enum whose discriminants and protobuf conversion match `kvrpcpb::CommandPri`. Add normal priority to both `TransactionOptions` constructors, add an idiomatic builder, and add setters on async and synchronous transaction/snapshot objects so priority can change after creation as in client-go. Extend the request abstraction once so every generated TiKV request can receive a priority. Route every read and write plan created by a transaction through that setting, including scan, pessimistic lock, heartbeat, prewrite, commit, rollback, and cleanup paths. Add tests that inspect dispatched protobuf contexts for normal, low, and high priority.

Then proceed through the ledger's dependency waves. Foundational value/config/error packages come before codec and request packages. Codec and RPC context come before region routing and client transport. Raw KV comes before the transactional stack. Observability and utilities are integrated with the production paths they affect. A package can span several Rust modules, but its Go package receipt remains atomic.

For each package, append a receipt to the ledger naming every Go source and test file, the Rust files that implement the behavior, deliberate non-applicable artifacts with reasons, exact validation commands, and the source commit. Do not mark `complete` when a dependent command, generated protobuf field, integration behavior, or fixture is missing.

## Concrete Steps

Work from `/Users/qiliu/projects/client-rust` unless a command explicitly names the Go source checkout.

For the first package, inspect all source evidence:

    sed -n '1,160p' /private/tmp/client-go/txnkv/txnutil/priority.go
    rg -n 'Priority|SetPriority' /private/tmp/client-go/txnkv/transaction /private/tmp/client-go/txnkv/txnsnapshot
    rg -n 'priority|CommandPri' src tests

After editing, run targeted formatting, unit tests, and lint:

    cargo fmt --all -- --check
    cargo test priority
    cargo test --lib
    cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

When the package is behaviorally complete, update both `Progress` and its ledger row in the same change. Record concise passing output and any test environment limitation.

For an integration-capable package, start a clean TiKV/PD playground, run the equivalent Go and Rust cases against it, capture only the relevant result transcript, and always stop the playground and remove its temporary data. Exact commands will be added to this plan before that milestone begins because the installed TiUP/TiKV versions must be pinned too.

## Validation and Acceptance

The first package is accepted when all three Rust priority values convert to the same protobuf values as Go; normal is the default; changing priority before or after transaction/snapshot creation affects subsequent read and write request contexts; sharding and retries preserve the context; async and sync wrappers expose the behavior; and targeted tests, full library tests, clippy, and rustfmt pass.

The full project is accepted only when every ledger row is `complete` or has a user-approved `not-applicable` receipt; all public raw and transactional operations supported by the pinned Go client have Rust equivalents or an explicitly approved compatibility adapter; differential tests pass against pinned TiKV and PD versions; generated protobuf inputs and outputs are accounted for; and release validation passes without unrecorded exclusions.

Compilation alone is never sufficient evidence for behavior parity.

## Idempotence and Recovery

Inventory and validation commands are read-only and safe to rerun. Formatting is deterministic. Test clusters must use dedicated temporary data directories and be stopped even after failures. If an implementation milestone fails, keep the ledger status at `seed` or `in-progress`; do not roll back unrelated user work. Source pins must not be moved silently—record a new decision and refresh affected receipts if either upstream revision changes.

The fork and local branch are recoverable from `origin/master` and `upstream/master`. Do not force-push or delete branches. Commits, when requested, must use DCO sign-off.

## Interfaces and Dependencies

For the first milestone, expose `tikv_client::Priority` with `Normal`, `Low`, and `High`, and convert it to `crate::proto::kvrpcpb::CommandPri`. `TransactionOptions` must provide a builder-style priority selector. `Transaction`, `Snapshot`, `SyncTransaction`, and `SyncSnapshot` must permit changing priority for future requests. `store::Request` must provide a priority-context setter implemented uniformly by every TiKV request generated in `src/store/request.rs`.

Do not add a new third-party dependency for this milestone. Use the already generated `kvrpcpb::CommandPri` and existing request context.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): unionstore's deterministic ART/RBT differential staging oracle now executes 4,000 mixed set/delete/nested-stage operations and validates every resulting map, length, size, iteration, and point read. Tonic's public client API is asynchronous while Rust Prometheus collectors are synchronous, and the workspace has no Channelz schema input. The ledger records this as a package-level integration decision requiring an explicit scrape-runtime/refresh contract; no incomplete cached collector is added.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added source `KeyLocation` bucket lookup semantics to the in-progress `internal/locate` mapping. The native `RegionWithLeader` distinguishes unrepresented stale bucket holes from out-of-region keys, preserves client-go's unclamped edge-hole fallback, and clamps only precise bucket metadata to region bounds. It is seed evidence only until bucket-aware range splitting and PD refresh paths consume it.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): introduced a cache-backed TiFlash-only selection and concrete PD route mapping. It preserves source pre-increment peer rotation, non-load-balanced peer retention, label eligibility, and TiKV/TiFlash candidate separation. BatchCop/MPP has no Rust request-plan consumer yet, and source failure-epoch, pending-peer, address, and compute-store lifecycle contracts remain attached to the incomplete `internal/locate` package.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): preserved PD pending-peer metadata with cached regions and added the source-ordered TiFlash all-valid/non-pending peer lists. This keeps the future BatchCop scheduling choice available without changing ordinary TiFlash route rotation; a request-plan consumer and store failure-epoch lifecycle are still required.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): preserved PD down-peer metadata and removed those peers from TiKV and TiFlash cache candidate sets before routing. This moves source `newRegion` filtering into the native cache representation; witness filtering and store failure epochs remain separate incomplete contracts.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the source witness-peer filtering slice: only the current witness leader may remain routable, and non-leader witnesses are omitted from TiKV/TiFlash selection and alternate-store lists. Store failure epochs and address re-resolution remain unfinished.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added explicit source `need_buckets` PD lookup variants through Cluster, RetryClient, and RegionCache. A bucket-aware lookup refreshes only entries whose cached metadata lacks buckets, preserving default PD traffic otherwise. Bucket-aware range splitting and asynchronous refresh de-duplication remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): started the atomic `internal/resourcecontrol` inventory and added native deterministic response accounting. Coprocessor and nested batch-task scan bytes and KV CPU now follow legacy/NextGen source rules; request-info extraction and interceptor integration remain owned by the incomplete dynamic tikvrpc/client boundary.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added typed Prewrite and Commit RequestInfo constructors with source write-byte totals and neutral read/write metadata. Generic tikvrpc wrapper extraction, bypass policy, PD controller invocation, and request/response interception remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed pipelined MemDB's source-specific `handleAlreadyExistErr` behavior. Flush workers now return a typed `PipelinedError`; a `KeyExistsError` is enriched from the immutable flushing generation before being returned, rather than being flattened to a string. Focused unionstore coverage includes the exact typed/error-value assertion.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed all eight production artifacts and six test/support/benchmark artifacts in the parent `internal/unionstore` package. The native core now includes source-compatible getter commit-timestamp options, unsupported-operation panics, value-history adapters, snapshot/concurrency mapping, pipelined metric observations, and source-scale ART/RBT differentials. The reusable UniStore crate remains an explicitly separate seed; public transaction consumption remains on `txnkv/transaction`.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): started the atomic `config/retry` milestone. Its complete inventory is `backoff.go`, `config.go`, `backoff_test.go`, and the goleak `main_test.go`; the existing Rust attempt-count `Backoff` is only seed evidence and must not be claimed until it adopts the source's budget, error, cancellation, clone/fork, and region-routing contracts.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the initial native `src/retry.rs` stateful backoffer beside the legacy public attempt-count helper. It now models every named source retry class, weighted and excluded cumulative budgets, per-class jitter state, rolling error records, cancellation, and `kv.Variables` kill handling. The package remains in progress pending exact clone/fork/update behavior, source metrics, region-error classification, and consumer migration.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the retry core's source clone/fork/update, independent child cancellation, `txnLockFast` per-sleep cap/reset, real-vs-fake region-error classification, source-labelled metrics, and distinct empty-message PD timeout terminal descriptor. The remaining gate is adoption by the Rust request/transaction retry paths and the owning integration packages; do not mark the package complete until those callers use the cumulative stateful budget.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected `config/retry`'s source diagnostic accounting: the bounded three-record diagnostic ring is now distinct from the lifetime `ErrorsNum` count and is copied/merged through clone/fork/update exactly as client-go tests require. The native backoffer now also exposes source-equivalent total type counts, variables, and fork ancestry type history; clone/fork intentionally clear `noop`, matching client-go's struct construction. The source excluded-class maximum is also covered: a class omitted from the ordinary budget still terminates after its separate limit. Eleven focused retry tests and whitespace validation pass on `nightly-2026-08-22`. The request layer remains explicitly unclaimed because all production retry loops still instantiate the legacy attempt-count `Backoff` per shard.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected the excluded-budget terminal-error selection. client-go's `longestSleepCfg` ignores excluded classes; when they alone exhaust their separate limit it returns the triggering operation error, not that class's configured static timeout. `RetryError::Exhausted` now represents this as `terminal: None` plus the preserved triggering reason, while non-excluded exhaustion retains the source static/PD terminal selection. The focused retry suite remains 11 passing tests on `nightly-2026-08-22`.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): started the atomic `internal/apicodec` milestone after completing its full inventory: production `codec.go`, `codec_v1.go`, `codec_v2.go`, and `mem_codec.go`; tests `codec_test.go`, `codec_v1_test.go`, and `codec_v2_test.go`. Native API-v2 construction now rejects numeric IDs above the source uint24 maximum, increments the complete mode-plus-ID prefix for unbounded range ends (including max-ID rollover), and writes the V2 keyspace ID to supported request contexts. The package remains in progress until reusable V1/V2 encode/decode primitives and every applicable cloned request/response transform are transcreated and integrated.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added public native `ApiV1Codec` and `ApiV2Codec` primitives plus API-version prefix parsing/splitting. They preserve source logical-versus-region memcomparable encoding, V2 reverse ranges, out-of-bound detection and overlap clipping, empty optional key handling, maximum-ID successor behavior, and V1 raw identity. Sixteen focused native tests and scoped lint pass; this is foundation work only, not the parent package receipt because command cloning and response error/lock transforms remain unimplemented.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): extended `ApiV2Codec` with the source `decodeRegionError`, `decodeKeyError`, lock, and MVCC helper behavior. Nested lock/deadlock/key-error fields decode in place; `EpochNotMatch` siblings wholly outside the current keyspace are removed while overlapping regions are clipped. Eighteen focused tests and scoped lint pass. Existing Rust response paths still use their earlier infallible truncation helpers, so this must be wired through each applicable response command before package completion.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added `KvRequest::decode_response` and invoked it at `Dispatch` immediately after typed transport response extraction, the source-equivalent point before retry/lock inspection. All 30 request-layer tests pass. Command-specific decoding remains pending because the protobuf context alone cannot distinguish numeric API V2 from Rust's API-v2-no-prefix embedding mode; the request/plan representation must retain that codec mode as it clones and shards requests.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): `Dispatch` now retains an optional numeric-V2 `ApiV2Codec`, derived by `PlanBuilder` from the request's raw/transaction mode and copied across shards. API V1 and API-v2-no-prefix deliberately retain no decoder, preserving source V1 ownership and Rust embedding pass-through semantics. The first supported transactional/raw Get response decodes V2 region/key errors at this dispatch boundary; all 31 request tests, scoped lint, and whitespace validation pass. Remaining command-specific decoder coverage is still required.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): expanded dispatch-time V2 error decoding across every currently supported transactional command: Get, BatchGet, Scan, ResolveLock, Prewrite, Commit, BatchRollback, PessimisticRollback, PessimisticLock, ScanLock, TxnHeartBeat, CheckTxnStatus, and CheckSecondaryLocks. It transforms region errors, standalone and per-pair key errors, and lock-bearing fields before retry/lock extraction; successful pair-key conversion remains on the existing high-level path until its atomic migration. Two focused transaction tests, 31 request tests, scoped lint, and whitespace validation pass. Raw command coverage and full successful-pair response migration remain pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added dispatch-time API V2 region/per-pair-error decoding for every currently supported raw request: Get, BatchGet, GetKeyTTL, Put, BatchPut, Delete, BatchDelete, DeleteRange, Scan, BatchScan, CAS, and RawCoprocessor. The raw batch regression verifies an `AlreadyExist` key decodes before error extraction while a successful pair key remains physical for the existing high-level transform. Five raw tests, 31 request tests, scoped lint, and whitespace validation pass. The remaining apicodec gate is atomic migration of successful response keys/ranges/locks and source command types absent from Rust's request surface.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): migrated raw `batch_get` successful pair keys atomically: its response decoder validates/decodes pair keys and the public method no longer strips an already-decoded prefix. Raw/keyspace tests (7 and 18 respectively), scoped lint, and whitespace validation pass. Transactional batch reads cannot use this shortcut because local-buffer pairs remain physical until `txnkv/transaction` performs its own coordinated buffer/response conversion; scan pagination likewise must preserve physical cursor keys until its owning scan path is migrated.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the V1 codec foundation's source-specific region-error transformation. `ApiV1Codec` now decodes transactional memcomparable `KeyNotInRegion` and `EpochNotMatch` bounds while retaining raw V1 identity; 19 focused keyspace tests, scoped lint, and whitespace validation pass. Routing V1 errors through Rust's region-cache path remains an integration decision on the request/region packages, not a completion claim for apicodec.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): integrated V1 region-error decoding at dispatch. Plan construction retains a V1 codec only for V1 requests, a V2 codec only for numeric API V2, and neither for V2-no-prefix; both codec fields survive shard cloning. Supported transactional/raw response implementations decode V1 `region_error` before retry handling, including raw batch get. Request/raw/transaction focused suites (32/5/2), scoped lint, and whitespace validation pass. Complete command/response inventory and keyspace-name context propagation are still pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added V1 and numeric-V2 dispatch decoding for the already-supported `UnsafeDestroyRangeRequest`, including its region error. Transaction/request focused suites (2/32), scoped lint, and whitespace validation pass. The generated-but-unowned Cleanup/GC/flashback/physical-scan/split/MVCC/raw-checksum/flush/buffer command surface remains explicitly pending rather than being conflated with this existing request-path integration.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated `BuildKeyspaceName`: empty configured keyspace names now canonicalize to `DEFAULT` before raw or transactional PD lookup. The helper and source default constant are public from `request`; 20 keyspace, 7 raw, and 69 transaction focused tests, scoped lint, and whitespace validation pass. Keyspace-name propagation into per-request Context and the unowned command matrix remain pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated `DecodeBucketKeys`. API V1 decodes each region key according to its raw/transaction memory codec; API V2 preserves source first/last outside-boundary empty markers and suppresses the duplicate empty prefix delimiter. Twenty-one focused keyspace tests, scoped lint, and whitespace validation pass. Bucket integration remains on the region-cache/request owning packages.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added source-equivalent V2 protobuf `encodeKeyRange` and `encodeKeyRanges` helpers. They clone caller ranges and expand empty ends to the keyspace successor; source-derived empty/start/end cases execute in the focused 21-test keyspace suite. Raw-checksum/coprocessor command ownership remains pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added V2 source helper mappings for cloned raw `KvPair`s, cloned transactional `Mutation`s, and coprocessor `KeyRange` encode/decode. Tests retain non-key pair metadata and validate an open coprocessor range round trip; the focused 21-test keyspace suite, scoped lint, and whitespace validation pass. Request command ownership/integration remains pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): full nightly regression checkpoint after the accumulated API-codec work passes all 206 `tikv-client` library tests, 2 standalone `unistore` tests, 49 `tikv-client` doctests, and `git diff --check`. This is regression evidence only: `internal/apicodec` remains in progress pending the complete source command matrix, keyspace-name Context propagation, and coordinated successful-response migration.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): raw-client keyspace metadata now follows client-go's codec-owned request context: construction retains PD's canonical keyspace name, all raw operations use one context-aware plan constructor, and the cloned API-V2 context test verifies the version, ID, and name together. Scoped raw and plan tests pass. The workspace Clippy gate under the newly pinned nightly is not currently usable as completion evidence because it reports 22 pre-existing unrelated lint violations; transactional and unowned-command context propagation remain pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transactional clients and transactions now retain PD's canonical API-V2 keyspace name through direct reads, scans, heartbeats, 2PC prewrite/commit/secondary commit, and rollback request plans. The source-derived regression captures a Get, Prewrite, and Commit request and verifies each has the same V2 version, keyspace ID, and name. Nested lock-resolution and cleanup subrequests are intentionally still pending: their plan wrappers currently carry only `Keyspace`, not canonical metadata.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed that nested request-context propagation. `PlanBuilder` retains keyspace metadata through merge/process/retry/shard/store/lock/cleanup transformations; `ResolveLock` and `CleanupLocks` carry it into the resolver, which applies it to CheckTxnStatus, CheckSecondaryLocks, ResolveLock, and BatchResolveLock plans. The lock regression captures CheckTxnStatus and ResolveLock after a lock response and verifies the original V2 version, numeric ID, and canonical name. Scoped lock/plan/transaction/raw suites pass; unsupported generated command ownership and the full source transform switch remain pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): migrated raw Scan and RawBatchScan successful `KvPair` keys to the source dispatch-time decoder. The raw client no longer performs a second high-level prefix truncation; its region-boundary pagination does not consume response keys, so the move preserves the cursor contract. Decoder tests cover both response types, and an end-to-end API-V2 scan test verifies physical request prefix/context and logical returned key.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the corresponding transactional BatchGet/Scan migration. Dispatch now fully decodes successful pairs; `transaction::Buffer` remains an intentional physical-key cache, so its fetch closures re-encode decoded remote pairs exactly once before cache merge and the public path retains its existing logical-key transform. The end-to-end regression captures physical V2 BatchGet/Scan requests and verifies both logical results, while keeping cache representations consistent. PessimisticLock has no successful key-bearing response field in client-go's codec switch; generated-but-unowned command types remain the separate response-transform work.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): full nightly regression after all request-context and successful-pair migrations passes 211 `tikv-client` library tests, 2 standalone `unistore` tests, 49 `tikv-client` doctests, and whitespace validation. This is a regression checkpoint only: `internal/apicodec` remains in progress because Go's complete command switch still spans generated request types not owned by the Rust request API, and `config/retry` remains in progress because replacing the public attempt-count retry configuration needs its own complete consumer/config migration.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): extended the owned API-codec command surface with legacy `GC` and transactional `DeleteRange`. Both now decode V1/V2 region errors; GC also decodes its lock-bearing key error. DeleteRange now uses the source-compatible V2 range transform, multi-region retry/sharding, and returns its successful completed-region count through `TransactionClient::delete_range`. The regression builds a real memcomparable region-error boundary, preventing point-key encoding from being mistaken for a region-boundary encoding. Focused transaction request/client suites and the nightly full regression pass: 212 `tikv-client` library tests, 2 `unistore` tests, 49 `tikv-client` doctests, and `git diff --check`. The remaining generated command matrix is still pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): integrated deprecated `Cleanup` exactly because it remains in client-go's API-v2 codec switch and `tikvrpc` command registry. The generated tonic method is now dispatchable; the request is transactional/single-key shardable and decodes V1/V2 region plus lock-bearing key errors before retry/lock extraction. A shared regression verifies Cleanup, GC, and DeleteRange error shapes. No new public client API was added because client-go documents Cleanup as unused since 4.0; its owning API boundary is the generated `tikvrpc` command layer.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): started the atomic `rawkv` milestone, whose audited source inventory is `rawkv.go`, `rawkv_test.go`, `test_prob.go`, plus raw integration support `integration_tests/raw/{api_mock_test.go,api_test.go,util_test.go,tikv-v1ttl.toml,tikv-v2.toml}`. Its first end-to-end command is `Checksum`: Rust now constructs one Crc64-XOR range request, shards/retries it by region, decodes V1/V2 region errors, XORs per-region checksums, sums key/value totals, and exports the source-compatible aggregate. Focused raw tests and the nightly full regression pass: 213 `tikv-client` library tests, 2 `unistore` tests, 49 `tikv-client` doctests, and `git diff --check`. This is seed evidence only; the full rawkv package, integration fixtures, and real-cluster validation remain required for its atomic receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected raw `BatchGet` to client-go's public result contract. `RawClient::batch_get` now returns one `Option<Value>` per supplied key in the same order, including duplicates; `None` represents absence and `Some(Vec::new())` represents a stored empty value. The former unordered existing-pair representation remains available as explicit `batch_get_pairs`. The API-V2 mock regression captures sorted physical request keys and request context, returns physical pair keys, and proves logical ordered/missing/empty/duplicate results after dispatch decoding. Final focused/full validation passes 214 `tikv-client` library tests, 2 `unistore` tests, 49 doctests, format, and `git diff --check`; the all-target integration/failpoint sweep was attempted but its eight real-cluster tests cannot start because PD is unavailable at `127.0.0.1:2379`.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected raw reverse-scan routing to use client-go's end-inclusive region semantics. `PdClient`, PD retry, and `RegionCache` now expose the generated PD `GetPrevRegion` route; the cache selects the previous region at an exact boundary. Raw reverse scans route each request from their moving upper bound, retain normalized lower/upper request construction, and advance through each selected region's start key. Source-derived regressions cover a two-region `[5,20)` scan with exact-boundary requests `(20,5)` then `(10,5)`, and direct cache boundary selection. Full nightly validation passes 216 `tikv-client` library tests, 2 `unistore` tests, 49 doctests, formatting, and `git diff --check`; the pre-existing global `mockRetryableErrorResp` failpoint race was made deterministic by placing its normal extractor test on the same serial test lock.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): RawKV column-family selection now preserves client-go's arbitrary string contract. `ColumnFamily` retains typed built-ins while representing any other name as `Custom(String)`; request construction writes that name unchanged to protobuf `cf`. The raw request regression sends `tenant_cf` through an API-V2 batch put alongside its keyspace context. Full nightly validation passes 217 `tikv-client` library tests, 2 `unistore` tests, 49 doctests, and `git diff --check`. This removes the previous Rust-only rejection of client-go's custom-CF test scenarios.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): Raw client atomic-CAS mode now has the full client-go boolean transition. The existing enable-only `with_atomic_for_cas` convenience method delegates to the new `with_atomic_for_cas_enabled(bool)` clone builder, so a derived client can restore normal writes and reject CAS after atomic mode had been enabled. Clone-only raw client configuration builders now apply to every `PdClient` implementation, allowing the source-derived mock transport regression to prove the later RawPut carries `for_cas = false`. Focused pinned-nightly format/test and whitespace validation pass; the full rawkv package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected RawKV `BatchPutWithTTL` argument semantics to match client-go. An empty TTL list now produces zero TTL for each pair, while both shorter and longer non-empty lists return the source error instead of Rust's previous panic/truncation behavior. The mock regression proves invalid inputs dispatch nothing and an empty TTL list sends `ttls = [0]`. Focused pinned-nightly format/test and whitespace validation pass; the full rawkv package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): removed Rust-only atomic-mode rejections for Raw `BatchDelete` and `DeleteRange`. Client-go sends both operations without a CAS-mode gate, and neither protobuf carries `for_cas`; the atomic-mode mock regression proves both dispatch normally, while the real-cluster raw CAS test now has the matching expectation. Focused pinned-nightly format/test and whitespace validation pass; the full rawkv package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated client-go's `DeleteRange(nil, nil)` multi-region regression at the raw request boundary. An unbounded Rust range now proves dispatch of the exact three mock intervals `([], [10])`, `([10], [250, 250])`, and `([250, 250], [])`, including the final open-ended shard. Focused pinned-nightly format/test and whitespace validation pass; the full rawkv package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the immutable Rust mapping for client-go's string-based `SetColumnFamily`: `with_cf_name` accepts arbitrary names and an empty name restores the default protobuf CF. The source-derived wire regression sends `tenant_cf`, then resets it and verifies the next request has `cf = ""`. Focused pinned-nightly format/test and whitespace validation pass; the full rawkv package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected RawGet, RawGetKeyTTL, and RawCAS response-error handling. Client-go returns each non-empty server `error` string; Rust now runs the existing error extractor before its value/TTL/CAS processors, preserving the native `MultipleKeyErrors([KvError])` contract. The mock regression verifies all three paths and source messages. Focused pinned-nightly format/test and whitespace validation pass; the full rawkv package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): full pinned-nightly regression after the accumulated RawKV fixes passes all 223 `tikv-client` library tests, 2 standalone `unistore` tests, 49 `tikv-client` doctests, and `git diff --check`. This is a regression checkpoint only: RawKV still needs all source integration artifacts and its final real-cluster validation decision, while `internal/apicodec` remains in progress behind unowned `tikvrpc` command integration.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the three-file `tikvrpc/interceptor` package (`interceptor.go`, `interceptor_test.go`, `main_test.go`). The native async interceptor receives the resolved target and immutable request, can wrap/replace the next transport dispatch, preserves chain flattening, duplicate-name replacement, and onion order, and is attached to every transaction/snapshot physical RPC including retries, commits, heartbeats, and lock-resolution subrequests. Rust's transaction/snapshot-owned plan state is the idiomatic replacement for Go's `context.Context` attachment. Focused chain and transaction regressions plus the full 225-test pinned-nightly library suite pass; no real cluster is required for the package's deterministic wrapper semantics.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): RawKV BatchPut now retains client-go's deprecated-but-wire-visible `RawBatchPutRequest.ttl` compatibility field as the first per-pair TTL, alongside the full `ttls` vector. The source behavior must survive sharding/retry reconstruction as well as initial construction; a captured two-TTL request now proves both fields (`ttl = 7`, `ttls = [7, 11]`). Focused pinned-nightly RawKV, format, and whitespace validation pass; the parent RawKV package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): RawKV now retains and exposes the PD cluster ID, matching client-go's synchronous `Client.ClusterID()` without an RPC per call. The connected PD retry client supplies the ID obtained during member validation; custom/mock PD implementations retain the source test default of zero. Clone-based RawClient configuration preserves it, covered by the atomic-mode clone regression. Focused pinned-nightly RawKV, format, and whitespace validation pass; `Close`/PD-handle lifecycle remain part of the raw-client transport integration audit.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected Rust RawKV reverse scans with an unbounded upper endpoint. Client-go documents that last-region discovery is unsupported but its `bytes.Compare` loop guard returns an empty successful result; Rust previously returned an error. `scan_reverse(lower.., limit)` and `scan_reverse(.., limit)` now return empty without dispatch, with a source-derived mock regression. The existing real-cluster integration expectations were changed from Rust's former full-range result to source-compatible emptiness and compile successfully (the cluster is not started locally). Focused pinned-nightly RawKV, format, and whitespace validation pass; the parent RawKV package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the ownership-safe native mapping for client-go `RawKVClient.GetPDClient()`. `RawClient::pd_client()` returns a cloned `Arc` of its routing/timestamp PD client, and the public `PdClient` trait is re-exported for consumers of that handle. The clone configuration regression verifies pointer identity across atomic-mode derivation, so the cluster ID and PD handle both remain stable. Focused pinned-nightly RawKV, format, and whitespace validation pass; Close/lifecycle behavior remains part of the transport audit.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the native consuming mapping for client-go `RawKVClient.Close()`. `RawClient::close(self)` drops this ownership handle; when it is the final owner, PD/TiKV channels and the PD timestamp-request sender are released, ending the background request stream. Derived Rust clients are independently shared handles, so they remain usable until their own close/drop. The lifecycle regression proves `close` releases the RawClient-held PD `Arc`; focused pinned-nightly RawKV, format, and whitespace validation pass.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the source `TestRawBatch` payload-boundary assertion at the request plan layer. Three 8 KiB RawBatchPut items in one mock region produce source-equivalent 16 KiB-plus-next-item batches of two and one pair; each captured request retains both the legacy first `ttl` and aligned `ttls`. This directly covers client-go `AppendBatches(rawBatchPutSize)` semantics without a live cluster. Focused pinned-nightly sharding, format, and whitespace validation pass.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): implemented client-go `rawkv.WithAPIVersion(APIVersion_V1TTL)`. `RawApiVersion::{V1,V1Ttl,V2}` is RawKV-only construction state; V1TTL retains the raw V1 PD/key codec, ignores any configured keyspace as client-go does, and—because client-go's final V1 codec encoder overwrites request contexts—sends `api_version = V1`, which V1TTL servers require. Both Get and the source's special-looking BatchPut path are captured at the wire boundary. Explicit V2 resolves either the supplied keyspace or PD's canonical `DEFAULT` keyspace; the existing `with_keyspace` convenience remains V2 under its default V1 setting. Focused configuration/keyspace/raw-wire regressions and the 16-test RawKV client suite pass on the pinned nightly. The parent RawKV package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated RawKV's source-specific `Context.max_execution_duration_ms` matrix. The request abstraction now attaches that server budget before sharding/retries. Raw BatchGet, BatchPut, Delete, BatchDelete, DeleteRange, and CAS carry client-go's fixed 20,000 ms write execution duration; ordinary Get, GetKeyTTL, and Put deliberately carry zero. The exhaustive captured-command regression and 15-test RawKV client suite pass on the pinned nightly; the full post-change checkpoint is 232 library tests and 50 doctests, with format and whitespace checks. The parent RawKV package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected RawKV atomic batch-delete wire behavior. Client-go constructs `RawBatchDeleteRequest.ForCas` from the client atomic flag; Rust previously allowed the operation but silently sent false. The lowering constructor and RawClient now retain the flag through its existing shard-clone path, while DeleteRange remains flagless as defined by its protobuf. Focused raw request/client suites pass on the pinned nightly; the post-correction full checkpoint is 233 library tests and 50 doctests, with format and whitespace checks. The parent RawKV package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected RawKV empty bounded DeleteRange handling. Client-go's `<` loop sends no RPC for `start == end` (or any reversed bounded range); Rust now makes the same decision on the logical `BoundRange` before API-V2 encoding turns an unbounded endpoint into a physical keyspace boundary. The no-routing/no-dispatch regression and 17-test RawKV client suite pass on the pinned nightly. The parent RawKV package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): repaired a Rust-specific request-context hole exposed during the `internal/apicodec` command audit. The custom, sharded `RawCoprocessorRequest` wrapper now forwards both keyspace name and maximum-execution-duration setters to its generated inner request, matching the generated request implementations and preventing V2 metadata from disappearing at the final dispatch boundary. The captured raw-coprocessor regression proves API V2, numeric keyspace ID, and keyspace name on the protobuf context; all 17 RawKV client tests pass on the pinned nightly. `internal/apicodec` remains in progress pending the full client-go command matrix and `tikvrpc` integration.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the direct native mappings for client-go's chainable, mutating `RawKVClient.SetColumnFamily(string)` and `SetAtomicForCAS(bool)`. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): audited the next retry integration boundary. Client-go `rawkv.go` constructs a 20,000 ms `config/retry.Backoffer` per public RawKV operation, forks it for concurrent batches, and merges the final no-longer-used fork with `UpdateUsingForked`; `config/retry/backoff.go` preserves cumulative sleeps, diagnostics, and class-specific exponential state. Rust already has a source-mapped `RetryBackoffer`, including fork/update accounting, but `RetryableMultiRegion` still accepts the legacy attempt-count `Backoff` and clones it independently for every shard. The migration must introduce an explicit request-plan retry-budget path and adopt it at RawKV call sites without changing existing public plan-builder behavior; no partial swap was made.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): implemented client-go `tikvrpc.Request.ToBatchCommandsRequest` as the typed native `BatchCommandRequest` conversion. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): implemented the paired client-go `FromBatchCommandsResponse` switch as typed `BatchCommandResponse::from_proto`. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): began the atomic `internal/client` milestone by recording its full source/support/test inventory. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the first source-derived internal-client dependency seed, `store::priority_queue`. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): audited `internal/client/client_collapse.go` and its source coverage in `client_test.go`. Request collapse is restricted to non-lite, non-batch `ResolveLock`, keyed by region ID, start version, and async flag; it copies mutable request state, shares only same-key in-flight work, and lets each waiter observe its own cancellation/timeout. It cannot be wired before the typed Rust client gains the owning dynamic command/request identity, sync/async client abstraction, and callback-executor/singleflight lifecycle from the rest of `internal/client`. No disconnected collapse mechanism was added.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): resolved the `internal/client/legacy_codec.go` implementation decision. That Go adapter exists only to force old grpc-go protobuf decoding because newer grpc-go returns input bytes to a shared pool after unmarshal. Rust's generated Prost messages own their decoded data and Tonic uses `ProstCodec`; neither exposes the borrowed-buffer assumption, so no Rust codec shim is required. This is an explicit not-applicable source-component decision, not a package-completion claim.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): audited `internal/client/conn_monitor.go`. Client-go polls each grpc-go `ClientConn` every second and exports one-hot connectivity-state gauges, clearing all labels on removal; `client.go` separately counts `TransientFailure` on request acquisition. Tonic's public `Channel` has no equivalent connectivity-state query, so Rust cannot truthfully emulate this component on the present abstraction. The internal-client transport design must expose a native connection-state source (or deliberately change transport implementation) before its pool/monitor receipt can be complete; no misleading no-op monitor or fabricated metric was added.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected a concrete existing transport mismatch in `internal/client/conn_pool.go`'s compression path. Client-go sends gzip only when validated `tikv-client.grpc-compression-type` is `gzip`; Rust previously always accepted gzip responses but never enabled gzip requests. `TikvConnect` now preserves its public default constructor, exposes a configuration-aware constructor, and sends gzip exactly for the source-selected setting. The focused connector regression passes; the parent `internal/client` package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected the paired gRPC keepalive configuration path. Client-go's `conn_pool` applies validated `GrpcKeepAliveTime` and `GrpcKeepAliveTimeout` as HTTP/2 gRPC pings on every TiKV connection; Rust previously hard-coded their defaults inside `SecurityManager`. `TikvConnect` now carries those durations from `Config.tikv_client`, and `SecurityManager::connect_with_keepalive` applies them through Tonic's `http2_keep_alive_interval` and `keep_alive_timeout` on both plaintext and TLS endpoints while preserving the old default helper for other callers. The regression proves default and non-default values; the parent `internal/client` package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the paired HTTP/2 flow-control configuration mapping from `internal/client/conn_pool.go`. `GrpcInitialWindowSize` and `GrpcInitialConnWindowSize` now travel from `Config.tikv_client` through `TikvConnect` and `SecurityManager` into Tonic's initial stream and connection window options for both TLS and plaintext endpoints. The focused connector regression captures custom settings; the parent `internal/client` package remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): hardened the flow-control conversion at the Go/Rust type boundary. Source settings are signed `int32` values, while Tonic expects optional unsigned sizes; Rust now maps nonpositive values to `None` (the transport default) rather than wrapping them into huge unsigned windows. The focused connector regression covers both explicit source-sized windows and the default fallback.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): audited the remaining live `TiKVClient` connector settings. Compression, HTTP/2 keepalive, and initial windows are now mapped. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): implemented the first real `GrpcConnectionCount` pool boundary.
